q: 1. Henry Gantt developed the bar chart technique in
explain: Henry Gantt devised his historical system of project progress charts around 1900–1915.

q: 2. The scheduled completion time of an operation in CPM chart is mentioned on
options: left top corner outside the circle
left top corner inside the circle
explain: Standard notation for event circles in CPM often places the earliest expected time at the top left outside the circle.

q: 3. Slack time refers to
explain: Slack time is associated with events (in PERT terminology) - the allowable time an event can be delayed.

q: 4. Which operation must complete first?
options: right of the line joining two circles
left of the line joining two circles
explain: In network logic, progress moves from left to right; therefore, activities on the left must be completed before those on the right.

q: 5. An event is
options: the start and/or finish of an activity or the group of activities
explain: An event marks the start and/or finish point of one or more activities; it is instantaneous and consumes no time.

q: 6. Gantt Bar chart is drawn for
explain: A Gantt chart explicitly plots individual activities (vertical axis) against time or duration (horizontal axis).

q: 7. Number of pre-operation associated with an operation may be
explain: An activity can have any number of preceding (pre-operation) tasks that must be finished before it starts.

q: 8. Bar chart is drawn for
explain: A bar chart plots activities against time, with bar length representing the duration of each activity.

q: 9. In a network, the activity which neither takes time nor resources is called
explain: A dummy activity (sometimes called redundant/null in specific contexts) is a logical link that uses zero time and zero resources.

q: 10. The maximum number of tail event occurring in a CPM is
explain: A standard project network should have only one single start event (tail event) from which the project begins.

q: 11. An activity requires
explain: An activity, by definition, is work that consumes both time and resources (manpower, material, equipment).

q: 12. The maximum number of head event occurring in a CPM is
explain: Similarly, a project network should converge to exactly one single end event (head event).

q: 13. Critical path method is an effective and powerful method of assessing
options: What tasks must be carried out
Where parallel activities can be performed
The shortest time in which you can complete a project
explain: CPM identifies required tasks, parallel activity opportunities, and the minimum project duration - covering all listed aspects.

q: 14. The maximum number of redundant activity in a CPM chart may be
explain: Depending on the complexity and poor logic of a network, any number of activities might be rendered redundant or unnecessary.

q: 15. Select the correct statement.
options: Activity arrows in a CPM network are drawn to scale
The tail of an arrow represents the finish of an activity
Arrow head represents the start of an activity
explain: None of the given statements is correct: arrows are not drawn to scale, the tail represents the start (not finish), and the head represents the finish (not start) of an activity.

q: 16. The activity which consumes maximum time is called
explain: The 'critical path' is the longest path, but a single activity consuming 'maximum time' is not a standard definition for a specific activity type in this context.

q: 17. A drawback of bar chart is
options: it is difficult to judge whether an activity is completed or not
all the activities represented are independent of each other
sequence of activities is not clearly defined
it is not possible to judge whether the activity is ahead or behind the schedule.
explain: The critical limitation of a standard bar chart is that it does not show logical dependency linkages or critical activity sequences.

q: 18. The number of post-activity associated with head event may be
explain: The final head event (end of project) has no subsequent activities (post-activities) following it.

q: 19. PERT is an abbreviation for
options: pertinent equation related to a task
explain: PERT stands for Program (Programme) Evaluation and Review Technique.

q: 20. The post-operations in CPM are marked
explain: In chronological flow, subsequent operations (post-operations) are placed to the right of the current task.

q: 21. CPM stands for
explain: CPM stands for Critical Path Method, a network-based project scheduling technique.

q: 22. In CPM method, the earliest finish is indicated by time on
options: top right, outside the circle, in triangle
top right, outside the circle, in rectangle
explain: The Earliest Finish Time (EFT) or Earliest Start Time (EST) is often noted in a square/rectangle near the event node.

q: 23. PERT is
explain: PERT networks are built around events (milestones) connecting activities, making PERT event-oriented.

q: 24. Latest finish time in CPM technique is indicated by
explain: Standard CPM notation uses rectangles (or squares) to denote time values like Latest Finish Time.

q: 25. CPM is
explain: CPM networks emphasize activities (jobs) and their durations, making CPM activity-oriented.

q: 26. When the times of earliest finish and the latest finish are equal in an operation, the operation is called
explain: If the earliest and latest times are equal, there is zero float, making that activity critical.

q: 27. PERT adopts
explain: PERT uses probability distributions (three time estimates) to account for uncertainty in activity durations, making it probabilistic.

q: 28. An example for a parallel activity is
options: completing ground floor and starting first floor
wall and carpentry work of doors and windows
completion of flooring and initiating white washing
digging of a well and of septic tank
explain: Parallel activities can happen simultaneously; wall construction and carpentry can often proceed at the same time in different sections.

q: 29. CPM adopts
explain: CPM uses a single fixed time estimate per activity, making it a deterministic approach.

q: 30. A dummy activity
options: had no tail event but had only a head event
had only a head event but no tail event
does not require any resources or any time
had no sequence and can be fitted anywhere
explain: A dummy activity is a purely logical connection used to show dependency without adding time or cost to the project.

q: 31. Which of the following statements is true?
options: PERT is activity oriented and adopts deterministic approach
CPM is event oriented and adopts probabilistic approach
CPM is activity oriented and adopts probabilistic approach
PERT is event oriented and adopts probabilistic approach
explain: PERT is indeed event-oriented and uses a probabilistic approach (three time estimates), correctly combining both characteristics unlike the other options.

q: 32. Critical path is
options: shortest path for the earliest completion of the project
longest path of the network from the first event to the last event
ideal path by preceeding along which the project can be completed as per the schedule
the path which takes into account the completion of all the parallel activities
explain: The critical path is the specific sequence of activities that must be completed exactly as scheduled to finish the project on time.

q: 33. Which of the following is an example of parallel activities?
options: construction of walls and casting of roof
construction of walls and carpentry work of doors and windows
casting of roof and construction of parapet wall
digging of well and construction of septic tank
explain: Wall construction and carpentry (doors/windows) work can proceed simultaneously without one depending on completion of the other, making them parallel activities.

q: 34. The minimum number of critical path in a net work should be
explain: Every project network must have at least one critical path connecting the start to the end.

q: 35. The occurrence of the completion of an activity is called its
explain: The head event marks the completion (ending point) of an activity in a network diagram.

q: 36. Critical path network helps the engineer to
options: concentrate his attention on critical activitirs
divert the different resourced from non-critical activities to critical activities
be cautious for avoiding any delay in the critical activities
explain: CPM analysis allows engineers to focus on the most important tasks and manage resources across the project efficiently.

q: 37. The occurrence of the starting of an activity is called its
explain: The tail event marks the starting point of an activity in a network diagram.

q: 38. In CPM, 'Forward Pass' and 'Backward Pass' are used to calculate respectively.
options: earliest expected time and latest allowable time
latest allowable time and earliest expected time
explain: Forward pass calculates Earliest times; Backward pass calculates Latest times.

q: 39. A dual role event
options: is the head event as well as a tail event
is the beginning of one event and the end of another
is any event other than the initial and final events
explain: A dual role event simultaneously serves as the head (completion) event of preceding activities and the tail (start) event of succeeding activities.

q: 40. A dummy activity
options: has no tail event but only a head event
has only head event but no tail event
does not require any resources or any time
has no bearing on the network and can appear anywhere
explain: A dummy activity is a fictitious link (zero duration, zero resource) used only to maintain logical sequencing between real activities.

q: 41. Positive float can occur when it is
explain: A sub-critical activity has a positive float, meaning it has extra time available and does not currently sit on the critical path.

q: 42. At an event other than final event if no activity emerges, it results in an error called
explain: Dangling occurs when an event (other than the final one) has no succeeding activity emerging from it, leaving it disconnected from the rest of the network.

q: 43. Negative float can occur when it is
explain: Negative float occurs in super-critical activities where the time required exceeds the time available, indicating the project is behind schedule.

q: 44. If the path of activities leads back into itself, the resulting error in the network is known as
explain: Looping is the network logic error where a sequence of activities forms a closed loop, violating the forward-progress requirement of a network.

q: 45. The estimated time required to complete an activity is termed as
explain: Duration is the standard term in project management for the estimated time needed to perform a specific task or activity.

q: 46. If the probability factor is zero, the chances of completing the project in scheduled time are;
explain: A probability factor (Z) of zero corresponds to the mean of the normal distribution, giving a 50% chance of completing within scheduled time.

q: 47. In PERT analysis, the start and end of event is represented by
explain: Events (nodes) in PERT mark the instantaneous starting or ending points of activities in the network diagram.

q: 48. Free float is mainly used to
options: identify the activities which can be delayed without affecting the total float of preceeding activity
identify the activities, which can be delayed without affecting the total float of succeeding activity
identify the activities which can be delayed without affecting the total float of either the preceeding or succeeding activities
explain: Free float is the amount of time an activity can be delayed without affecting the earliest start time of any immediately following (succeeding) activities.

q: 49. In PERT, the critical path represents the
options: shortest path for the earliest completion of the project
longest path of the network from the initial to final event
ideal path by proceeding along which the project can be completed as per schedule
path which takes into account the completion of the parallel activities
explain: The critical path is defined as the longest path through the network from start to finish, determining minimum project duration.

q: 50. Whenever activity has zero total float, then
options: free float of the activity must be zero but independent float need not be zero
independent float must be zero but free float need not be zero
free float and independent float both must be zero
free float and independent float both need not be zero
explain: Since total float is the 'parent' float, if it is zero, all other sub-types of float (free and independent) must also be zero.
